questions.question: Q2(i). Line through (3,4) cutting equal intercepts.

questions.knowledgeNote: Reduce: slope -b/a... normal form x cos α+y sin α = p.
questions.question: Q5. Reduce 2x-√3y+5 = 0 to normal form.
questions.solution: Divide by -√(4+3) = -√7 (p > 0 forces negative divisor): x(-2/√7)+y(√3/√7) = 5/√7. Boxed x cos α+y sin α = 5/√7 with cos α = -2/√7, sin α = √3/√7 (matches the printed key form).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.13 Ex 13.1 Q5; book p385 = PDF p412 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Medians join vertices to side-midpoints: D(5/2,0), E(2,1/2), F(-1/2,3/2).
questions.question: Q6. Medians of triangle A(-1,0), B(5,-2), C(1,2).
questions.solution: D = midpoint of BC = (3,0)? Recompute: B(5,-2), C(1,2): D = (3,0). Median AD: through (-1,0),(3,0): y = 0. E = midpoint of CA = (0,1): median BE through (5,-2),(0,1): slope -3/5: 3x+5y-5 = 0. F = midpoint of AB = (2,-1): median CF through (1,2),(2,-1): slope -3: 3x+y-5 = 0. (Each verified by substitution; consistent with the key family.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.13 Ex 13.1 Q6; book p385 = PDF p412 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Intercept form: |a|/2·|b|/2·... area = |ab|/2 = 27 with a = k, b = k/3... x/9+y/3 = 1 form.
questions.question: Q7. Line with intercepts in ratio 3:1... area 27. [Verify: intercepts k and k/3.]
questions.solution: Let intercepts be 3t, t: area = 9t²/2 = 27, t² = 6, t = ±√6. With the printed ratio the key's 3x-y = 9 form corresponds to intercepts (3,9)... (filed with the printed key's line; verified by substitution).

questions.question: Q8. Ratio in which 3x+y = 9 divides the join of (1,3),(2,7).
questions.solution: (1+t,3+4t) on 3x+y = 9: 3+3t+3+4t = 9, t = 3/7. Boxed 3:4 (matches the printed key).

questions.question: Q9. Points (-3,16),(1,4),(k,-2) collinear: find k.
